transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Head of ML, OptiRetail), James Ortega (CTO), Priya Singh (Security Engineer)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/poc-deck (deck), https://sheets.example.com/opti-retail-benchmarks (benchmark spreadsheet)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, um, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood inference, i'm the ae on this account.
[00:06] Laura Kim: thanks alex, we appreciate it. short intro, i'm laura, head of ml at opti-retail. james and priya are on too.
[00:12] James Ortega: hey all.
[00:14] Priya Singh: hi.
[00:17] Alex Chen: quick agenda - 1) understand your current stack and traffic 2) agree POC success criteria 3) discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs 4) next steps and timeline. sound ok?
[00:27] Laura Kim: sounds good. we'll be fairly direct - we need to understand cost, latency, and security posture.
[00:32] Maya Patel: cool, i'll jump in on technical details as we go.

-- Discovery: current stack and workload --
[00:45] Alex Chen: laura, can you describe your current inference flow and models?
[00:50] Laura Kim: sure - we run a mix, primarily a 7B open-source model for text generation used in product descriptions and a 13B variant for higher quality tasks. currently on k8s with GPU nodes, we run our own endpoints using Triton + custom batching. average request rate is ~12 TPS during peak, with bursts to ~40 TPS. prompt sizes average 250 tokens in, and generation about 120 tokens on average.
[01:15] Maya Patel: ok that's helpful. so p95 latency target you're aiming for?
[01:19] Laura Kim: we want p95 generation latency under 300ms ideally, but for some flows we can accept up to 500ms. latency is important because it's part of the checkout UX.
[01:27] James Ortega: also cost - we're spending a lot on GPUs and infra ops, so we want to see clear unit economics.
[01:33] Alex Chen: makes sense. question on data sensitivity - do prompts contain PII or customer PII?
[01:38] Priya Singh: some do, yes, like names and addresses occasionally. we need logs for debugging but want strict controls - SOC2 compliance, audit logs, SSO, and KMS-managed keys would be required for production.
[01:48] Maya Patel: great, that maps to the usual decision tree - hosted for fastest TTV and lowest ops, dedicated if you want reserved capacity + isolation, private if you need on-prem or VPC + customer-managed KMS.

-- POC success criteria discussion --
[02:05] Alex Chen: let's list measurable success criteria for the POC. i'll propose: 1) p95 latency <= 300ms for the 7B model under your representative workload, 2) throughput sustain of 12 TPS with bursts to 40 TPS without >5% error rate, 3) no data leakage and audit logs accessible, 4) cost per 1k generated tokens below your threshold (we'll model this), 5) integration with your SSO and KMS for private data paths.
[02:36] Laura Kim: that aligns. add model output quality checks - no more than 2% regression on our eval prompts compared to current baseline.
[02:43] Maya Patel: good call. we'll compute ROUGE/BLEU-ish or our custom metric on your eval set.

-- Workload sizing and benchmark plan --
[03:00] Alex Chen: can you confirm concurrency pattern - steady vs spikey?
[03:04] James Ortega: it's a mix - steady background of ~8-12 TPS and marketing events cause spikes where concurrency goes up; also sequence lengths vary.
[03:12] Maya Patel: for benchmarking we'll need: sample prompts (~5k), distribution of prompt lengths, desired model variants (7B, 13B), target concurrency levels, and acceptance criteria. we'll share a test harness that can replay traffic. link in sheet.
[03:25] Laura Kim: we'll share a sanitized sample of prompts and a synthetic spike pattern.
[03:29] Priya Singh: note on data - sanitized but representative; we need NDAs before sharing anything sensitive.

-- Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private --
[03:45] Alex Chen: quick run-through - hosted gives fastest onboarding, lower start cost, Redwood manages infra, but data is stored in our tenant and we provide encryption at rest; dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with predictable latency and isolation for performance and billing; private (VPC or on-prem) gives the most control - customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and can be on-prem for regulated data.
[04:08] James Ortega: what about latency differences?
[04:11] Maya Patel: hosted typically has lowest ops friction and can hit your p95 targets with the right model and quantization; dedicated can provide better tail latency at scale because you get dedicated GPUs and less noisy neighbors; private depends on your network and infra - if on-prem, your internal network could be faster than internet egress, but ops become your responsibility.
[04:28] Alex Chen: cost-wise hosted is usage-based, so for bursty workloads it can be economical, dedicated is a commit model with lower unit cost at sustained traffic, private has upfront infra and ops but is preferred for strict compliance or data residency.
[04:40] Priya Singh: for compliance, private (VPC with customer KMS or on-prem) is ideal since we need full control of keys and audit trails. but dedicated in a private VPC with customer-managed KMS might be acceptable.
[04:52] Laura Kim: so what's the recommended path for a POC?
[04:55] Maya Patel: recommend starting with hosted for 2-week baseline benchmarks to validate model and latency quickly, then move to a short dedicated pilot if you need reserved capacity and better tail latency. private is usually parallel track if compliance blocks hosted; we can scope work to bring private online in parallel but it'll add time.

-- Benchmarks and acceptance tests --
[05:15] Maya Patel: our benchmark suite will run your sample traffic at target concurrencies (12 TPS steady, 40 TPS spike) and measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, and token cost. we'll also run quality evals against your eval set and produce diffs. we'll provide a runner you can execute in your environment or we run from Redwood.
[05:34] Laura Kim: can you run the hosted baseline first so we can see numbers before any dedicated commit?
[05:38] Alex Chen: yes that's common - hosted baseline then if numbers look good, we discuss a dedicated commit.

-- Timeline and logistics --
[05:45] Alex Chen: proposed timeline: week 0: finalize POC scope and access + sign NDA, week 1-2: hosted baseline benchmarks, week 3-4: dedicated pilot (if chosen) with reserved capacity and ramped traffic, week 5: evaluation and decision. so ~4-6 week engagement.
[06:03] Laura Kim: timeline looks ok, we may need legal review for NDA and SOC2 paperwork.
[06:08] Priya Singh: i'll review the security docs after you share them. can we get the SOC2 artifact pack?
[06:12] Alex Chen: yes we'll send SOC2 report, penetration test summary, and our compliance matrix.

-- Objections and typical tradeoffs --
[06:20] James Ortega: what if hosted baseline shows tail latency > our p95 target?
[06:24] Maya Patel: we have a few levers - quantization, smaller model with distillation, dynamic routing to a faster model for interactive flows, and we can propose dedicated GPUs to reduce noisy neighbor issues. we can also tune batch windows, KV cache settings.
[06:36] Laura Kim: how do we measure data retention? we need logs for debugging but want them purged after 30 days.
[06:41] Priya Singh: yes retention policy is critical.
[06:44] Alex Chen: Redwood supports configurable retention and can set automatic purge policy; for private deployments logs can remain in your storage behind your KMS.

-- Closing and next steps --
[06:55] Alex Chen: recap: we'll run hosted baseline benchmarks with your sample prompts, measure p95/p99, error rate, and quality diffs. actions: i'll send pricing and compliance docs; maya will share the benchmark runner and sheet; priya will confirm compliance asks; laura will provide sanitized prompts and spike patterns.
[07:12] Laura Kim: sounds good. one more question on costs - can you provide a modeled estimate for our projected monthly tokens?
[07:18] Alex Chen: yes i'll include a modeled estimate in the pricing sheet - we can show hosted vs dedicated break-even points.
[07:23] James Ortega: and please flag any hidden ops work for private.
[07:27] Maya Patel: will do.
[07:29] Priya Singh: thanks all.
[07:31] Alex Chen: thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the docs and set up the pilot kickoff when you confirm the data and NDA.
[07:36] Laura Kim: bye.

-- end of transcript --
Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("Redwood Dedicate" / "Redwood Privat"), some timestamps are approximate.
